THE REALM
Ethiopia and the places of the account
The nations. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of her
Philip met “a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch of great authority under Candace queen of the Ethiopians, who had the charge of all her treasure, and had come to Jerusalem for to worship”. Acts 8:27
From the textShe does not appear in the story herself; Acts names her only to say whose officer he was. Acts 8:26–39
DEALINGS
Dealings with God's people
Her treasurer had come to Jerusalem to worship, and was reading the book of Isaiah. Acts 8:27–28
He “had the charge of all her treasure”. Acts 8:27
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE
No years given
No year is given. Acts tells the story after Stephen's death and the scattering of the church from Jerusalem (Acts 8:1–5). Which queen reigned then is not known from the sources used here.
A title borne by a line of queens
Pliny, Natural History 6.35 (about AD 77); ISBE (1915), “Candace”
Pliny reports that the name had “passed from queen to queen for many years”; the ISBE (1915) follows him: the name had “already been borne for many years by the queens of Ethiopia”.[33][20]
Acts uses it as a name
Our reading of Acts 8:27
Acts writes “Candace queen of the Ethiopians”, as one would a name with a title, and gives no other name. Acts 8:27
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 1
Acts 8
PASSAGES · 1
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not give her own name, if “Candace” is a title, nor her dates.
Scripture does not say whether she heard of her treasurer's baptism.
Acts does not say where in “Ethiopia” she reigned; Meroë and Napata come from Pliny and Strabo.
What the eunuch did on returning home is not in Scripture; Irenaeus and Eusebius report it, Eusebius with “is said”.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textScripture names her once, to say whose treasurer the eunuch was. Whether “Candace” was her own name or a title is a question below. Acts 8:27
